name: RSS2Post – AI RSS Feed to Post Autoblogger
author: Samuel Bezerra

sections.description:
RSS2Post turns the articles in an RSS feed into new blog posts on your WordPress site.

You paste your feed URLs, tick the articles you like and click Generate. For each one, the RSS2Post service writes a new article in your language and publishes it on your site with a featured image, categories and tags. You do not need an AI account or an API key.

See it in 50 seconds:

How it works

  1. Add your feeds. Paste one or more RSS feed URLs, one per line, and click “Parse News & Select Articles”. WordPress reads the feeds and lists the latest articles.
  2. Pick the articles. Tick the ones you want. Articles that look like a post you already have are flagged, so you do not publish the same story twice.
  3. Click Generate. Each article is rewritten as a new post and published on your site. When it finishes you get the links to the new posts.

What each post gets

  • A new article, not a copy of the feed item. Links back to the source site are removed.
  • A featured image: a free stock photo from Pexels that fits the topic, or the image from the feed. You can also turn images off.
  • WebP images (optional), so pages load faster.
  • Categories: the ones you always want, plus other categories of your site that fit the article.
  • Tags picked from the tags your site already uses.
  • A link to a related post already on your site, when there is one.
  • Your language: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish or Finnish.

Autopilot (Pro)

Switch on Automated Posting and RSS2Post checks your feeds by itself and publishes new posts every day. You choose how many times a day it runs and how many articles it publishes a day (up to 10). When you use several feeds, they take turns, so one busy feed does not take all the slots.

Also included

  • Generation history: a list of the posts RSS2Post created, with links.
  • Auto-delete old posts (optional): moves posts older than the age you choose (2 weeks to 1 year) to the trash. Useful for news sites. It is off by default, and it applies to all posts on the site, so read the note in the settings before you switch it on.

Who is it for?

  • News and niche blogs that want to cover what is happening in their topic every day
  • Site owners who want to keep a blog active without writing every post themselves
  • Agencies that run content sites for clients

Free and Pro

  • Free: 10 articles, to try everything except Automated Posting. No card needed.
  • Pro ($19.90 per month): unlimited articles, Automated Posting and priority support. You upgrade from the plugin page and pay through Stripe. You can cancel at any time.

Good to know

RSS2Post is a tool: you choose the feeds and you are responsible for what you publish. Use feeds you are allowed to use, and read the posts, especially at the start. AI can make mistakes.

External services

RSS2Post needs external services to work. Nothing is sent until you generate posts, switch on Automated Posting or start an upgrade.

RSS2Post service

The articles are written and published by the RSS2Post service at https://rss2post.fly.dev, run by the plugin author. It writes the article with AI (OpenAI models and a model hosted by the service), finds an image and publishes the post on your site through the WordPress REST API.

What is sent: the articles you selected (title, summary, link and image URL), your site URL, your WordPress username and application password (used to publish the post), your WordPress user ID and email address (used to identify your plan), your categories and most used tags, the language and image settings, and your Pexels API key if you entered one.
When: when you click Generate, when Automated Posting runs (Pro), when you start an upgrade and when the plugin checks your plan.
Terms and privacy: the service uses this data only to create and publish your posts and to manage your plan. Article text is sent to OpenAI to be written: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use and https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

Pexels

When Pexels is the image source, the service searches Pexels for a free stock photo that fits the article.

What is sent: search words taken from the article.
When: when a post is generated with Pexels as the image source.
Terms of Service: https://www.pexels.com/terms-of-service/
Privacy Policy: https://www.pexels.com/privacy-policy/

Stripe

Pro subscriptions are paid through Stripe. RSS2Post never sees or stores your card.

What is sent: your email address and WordPress user ID, to create the checkout. You enter your payment details on Stripe’s page.
When: only when you click Upgrade.
Terms of Service: https://stripe.com/legal
Privacy Policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Privacy

The plugin does not track visitors of your site and adds nothing to your public pages. The data listed under “External services” is sent only for the purposes described there. Your WordPress login password is never asked for or sent: the plugin uses an application password, which you can revoke at any time under Users → Profile.

Support

For questions, ideas or bug reports, use the plugin support forum on WordPress.org or GitHub: https://github.com/samukbg/Rss2Post

Technical Requirements

  • WordPress 5.6 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • A site that is public on the internet over HTTPS, with the WordPress REST API enabled
  • WP-Cron (or a real cron job) for Automated Posting
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “RSS2Post”, then click Install and Activate.
  2. Open “Rss to Post” in the admin menu.
  3. In section 1, enter your WordPress username and an application password, then click Save Credentials. To create an application password, click “Generate Application Password” (or go to Users → Profile → Application Passwords), type a name such as “RSS2Post” and click “Add New Application Password”.
  4. In section 2, paste your RSS feed URLs, one per line.
  5. Click “Parse News & Select Articles”, tick the articles and click Generate.

Optional: choose the image source, the categories and the language in sections 3 to 5 first.
sections.faq:
Do I need an OpenAI key or any other AI account?

No. The writing is done by the RSS2Post service. The free plan includes 10 articles. Pro is unlimited.

Why does it ask for an application password?

The RSS2Post service publishes the finished post on your site through the WordPress REST API, and it needs permission to do that. An application password is a separate password made by WordPress for one tool. It is not your login password, and you can revoke it at any time under Users → Profile.

The post was not published. What should I check?

Check that the username and application password are correct, that your site is public on the internet over HTTPS (it cannot publish to a site on your own computer), and that a security plugin or firewall is not blocking the WordPress REST API.

Are the posts copies of the original articles?

No. Each post is a new article written from the title and summary of the feed item. Links to the source site are removed. You are still responsible for what you publish, so read the posts and use feeds you are allowed to use.

Where do the images come from?

You choose: free stock photos from Pexels, the image from the RSS item, or no image. For Pexels you can add your own free Pexels API key, or leave the field empty to use the shared one.

How does Automated Posting work?

It is a Pro feature. Add your feeds, save your credentials, switch on Automated Posting and set how many times a day it runs and how many articles it publishes a day. It uses the WordPress scheduler (WP-Cron), so your site needs visits or a real cron job for it to run on time.

Will it publish the same article twice?

It remembers the feed items it already used. When you pick articles by hand, items that look like a post you already have are flagged with a warning.

Can I write posts in another language than the feed?

Yes. Pick the language in Content Settings. The post is written in that language even if the feed is in another one.

How do I cancel Pro?

There is no cancel button in the plugin yet. Open a topic in the support forum and we will cancel it for you. Never post payment details in the forum.

1.2.5

  • Feature: Added automatic internal link injection to related articles.
  • SEO: Prevent generation of duplicate post titles.
  • SEO: Prevent truncated/malformed slugs by relying on WordPress native generation.
  • SEO: Prevent thin or empty content from being published.
  • SEO: Control tag bloat by limiting tags generated to top 30 existing site tags.

1.2.4

  • Feature: Added Refresh Status button with cache bypassing mechanism.

1.2.3

  • Bug Fix: Fix whitelist verification logic and batch auto-delete mechanism.

1.2.2

  • Compatibility: Confirmed compatibility and updated “Tested up to” for WordPress 7.1.

1.2.1

  • ENHANCEMENT: Added Post2Podcast promotion to the settings page.

1.2.0

  • ENHANCEMENT: Version bump for UI improvements.

1.1.9

  • Feature: Added an “Auto-Delete Old Posts” feature to automatically clean up older posts generated by the plugin based on configurable time intervals.

1.1.8

  • UI/UX: Revamped the plugin admin dashboard with a modern “Soft UI Evolution” aesthetic, improving contrast, spacing, and visual hierarchy for a premium feel.

1.1.7

  • Feature: Added a multiple-link list feature for integrating affiliate links or referral codes contextually inside the generated articles.

1.1.6

  • Improvement: General improvements and minor fixes.

1.1.5

  • Fix: Restored missing JavaScript function for updating the generation button.
  • Improvement: Enhanced frontend UI stability.

1.1.4

  • Improvement: Implemented asynchronous job system with polling for more reliable content generation.
  • Improvement: Enhanced connection handling to ensure stable communication with the backend service.
  • Security: Further isolated service configurations to improve security and ease of use.
  • Performance: Optimized generation workflow for faster and more consistent results.

1.1.3

  • Feature: Added customizable automated posting frequency and article limits per day.
  • Feature: Added article size option (Small, Medium, Long) for content generation.
  • Improvement: Enhanced tag handling to use existing tags instead of creating new ones.
  • Improvement: Automated posting now intelligently distributes articles throughout the day based on user settings.

1.1.2

  • Resolved PHP fatal error due to function redeclaration.
  • Updated plugin version and minor improvements.

1.0.8

  • Updated plugin version and minor improvements.

1.0.7

  • CRITICAL FIX: Automated posting now works correctly with Run Now and toggle features
  • Fixed bug where “Run Now” button in WP Cron Events did not post any content
  • Fixed bug where disabling/re-enabling automated posting did not trigger immediate posting
  • CRITICAL FIX: RSS feeds now post reliably across all cycles
  • Fixed critical GUID tracking bug that prevented feeds from posting after first cycle
  • Plugin now only marks articles as “processed” after they are successfully posted
  • Feeds that don’t post in one cycle will now correctly post in the next cycle
  • Enhanced logging to track which feeds successfully posted articles
  • NEW: Post2Podcast cross-promotion section – Discover our companion podcast creation plugin

1.0.6

  • Implemented round-robin article distribution: Automated posting now fairly distributes articles across all RSS feeds
  • Fixed issue where high-frequency feeds would dominate the posting queue
  • Articles are now selected in rotation: Feed1→Feed2→Feed3→Feed1→Feed2→Feed3, ensuring equal representation
  • Enhanced logging to show which feed each article comes from
  • Maximum 6 articles per automated run, distributed evenly across all configured feeds

1.0.5

  • Fixed automated posting RSS feed sync bug: Automated posting now correctly processes all RSS feed URLs, not just the first one
  • Added automatic RSS feed synchronization when feeds are modified while automation is enabled
  • Improved feed management with real-time updates to automated posting configuration
  • Enhanced logging for automated feed updates to help with debugging
  • Users no longer need to toggle automation off/on when adding new RSS feeds

1.0.4

  • Fixed Stripe payment redirect security issue
  • Replaced nonce-based validation with proper Stripe session verification
  • Improved payment flow reliability for both test and production modes
  • Enhanced security validation for payment redirects
  • Better error handling for invalid payment sessions

1.0.3

  • Fixed WordPress.org review compliance issues
  • Updated contributor username for proper plugin attribution
  • Upgraded Stripe PHP library to latest version (v17.5.0) for security
  • Removed inline JavaScript and implemented proper wp_enqueue_script patterns
  • Added comprehensive external services documentation (Pexels API, AI service, Stripe)
  • Enhanced security with proper nonce verification for all user inputs
  • Improved data sanitization using WordPress best practices
  • Fixed potential security vulnerabilities in GET/POST parameter handling

1.0.0

  • Initial release with full feature set
  • AI-powered content generation
  • Multi-language support (18+ languages)
  • Advanced image handling with Pexels integration
  • WebP image conversion support
  • Automated posting for Pro users
  • Stripe payment integration
  • Duplicate detection system
  • Generation history with pagination
  • WordPress plugin compliance improvements
  • Enhanced subscription synchronization
  • Serviceware model implementation
